sources.title: GPT-5.5 Pro gold-standard harness product doctrine synthesis

requirements.summary: Harness Ultragoal is a productized agentic engineering harness; law-bearing surfaces must improve execution, verification, observability, repair, reliability, or claim integrity.
Gate 92 is the agent sensory system and must cover metrics, traces, wide events, logs, evals, product/system health, and agent quality.
Telemetry must carry agent, tool, repo, eval, command, law, claim, repair, duration, worker, cache, saturation, redaction, and boundedness attributes while keeping metric labels bounded.
Real command failures must support same-candidate query and explain output that tells an agent what failed, why, where, what claim is blocked, and the smallest repair.
Failed traces, opaque output, bad repairs, slow workflows, corrections, near misses, stale evidence, and claim theater must become feedback, evals, fixtures, laws, or blockers.
AGENTS.md and setup or retrofit outputs must act as routing tables to canonical CLI commands, telemetry, evals, architecture, security, privacy, and quality gates.
Tools, adapters, model calls, live probes, setup helpers, and external writers must declare risk tier, approval, schemas, telemetry, failure semantics, and claim impact.

Product truth, observability truth, and artifact truth must be cross-linked but non-substitutable across receipts, runtime behavior, live observability, source proof, install proof, and final packets.

Gate 105 must measure system health and agent quality using same-surface telemetry for diagnosis time, repair time, reruns, stale evidence recurrence, opaque failures, claim theater, manual spelunking, entropy cleanup, eval trend, latency, and lane regressions.

evidence_anchors.source_signal: The synthesis defines Harness Ultragoal as a productized agentic engineering harness whose laws must improve agent work rather than only generate receipts.
The synthesis makes Gate 92 the agent sensory system with metrics, traces, wide events, logs, evals, system health, and agent quality planes.
The synthesis requires an expanded telemetry envelope and cardinality doctrine that keeps high-cardinality values queryable without unbounded metric labels.
The synthesis requires same-candidate query and explain output that identifies root cause, affected claims, implicated artifacts, and the narrow repair.
The synthesis requires repeated failures and corrections to be harvested into feedback, evals, regression fixtures, standards rows, laws, or blockers.
The synthesis treats AGENTS.md and setup outputs as routing tables to canonical command, telemetry, eval, architecture, security, privacy, and quality surfaces.
The synthesis requires every tool and adapter surface to declare risk tier, approval boundary, schemas, telemetry, failure semantics, and claim impact.
The synthesis separates product truth, observability truth, and artifact truth so receipts, spool files, source proof, live behavior, and final packets cannot substitute for one another.
The synthesis requires Gate 105 to measure system health and agent quality with same-surface telemetry instead of anecdotes or cherry-picked runs.

sources.title: Gold-standard stack developer-experience and governance archive

requirements.summary: The repository, runtime harness, validation system, observability stack, eval suite, and cleanup system are product surfaces; tool presence alone is not compliance.
Rust, TypeScript, Python, SQL, infrastructure, telemetry, and tools emit observations only; ultragoal converts observations into claims through typed same-surface evidence.
A fresh agent must discover setup, validation, local runtime, evals, and release proof from repo files only; hidden local state cannot support claims.
Every source, package, install, runtime, browser, database, workflow, observability, and product claim must be proven on its same surface.
Cargo, Bun, uv, Nix, OpenTofu, and equivalent lockfiles are governed truth surfaces; lock drift blocks dependent build, package, release, and update_goal claims.
No trace, metric, log, event, or eval record may introduce unregistered attributes; each attribute has type, owner, cardinality, privacy, and allowed surfaces.
Every tool or MCP action requires typed schemas, risk class, approval policy, idempotency class, telemetry span, cleanup policy, and claim impact.
Agent work must be inspectable through a cockpit or equivalent runtime surface showing plans, diffs, validations, traces, evals, tool calls, artifacts, and claim ceilings.
Every generated artifact, cache, package, install copy, database state, trace, media artifact, receipt, packet, lock, pid, port, and tempdir must be classed before cleanup.
update_goal is forbidden unless the CLI verifies current goal state, active receipts, stack claim ceiling, product proof eligibility, and cleanup/protection status.
ultragoal stack fast is the hot inner loop and supports only fast feedback plus changed-scope structural observations, not review, release, product, or update_goal claims.
ultragoal stack standard is the serious source-local repair proof loop covering language standards, migrations, observability semantics, tool inventory, fixtures, receipts, and claim ceiling.
ultragoal stack release is the full release/product proof loop and supports release/product/final-packet claims only when every same-surface receipt is current.
ultragoal stack clean-proof --cache-mode none proves clean checkout and no hidden cache dependence through isolated caches, tool bootstrap, local services, and the standard loop.
ultragoal stack watch emits observations only and cannot mint completion claims without current receipt verification and claim-ceiling computation.
ultragoal stack resources prove must cover bounded memory, queues, processes, pools, browser artifacts, workflow backlog, and agent tool cleanup across the stack.
ultragoal gc plan, dry-run, apply, and verify govern cleanup; blind deletion and unclassified artifact removal cannot support claims.
Stack receipts must record command, goal, git and worktree state, toolchain identities, surface digests, component receipts, claim support/exclusions, issue time, expiry, and staleness triggers.
Cache use is legal but cache concealment is illegal; warm-cache speed is not clean-checkout proof and cache proof supports only cache-surface claims unless a same-surface law allows more.

evidence_anchors.source_signal: The archive states the repository, runtime harness, validation system, observability stack, eval suite, and artifact cleanup are first-class product surfaces.
The archive states observations from languages, tools, infrastructure, and telemetry become claims only after ultragoal binds typed current same-surface evidence.
The archive requires setup, validation, local runtime, evals, and release proof to be discoverable from repo files without hidden author memory.
The archive maps each proof surface to its own evidence class and rejects package, rollout, trace, metric, or reviewer substitutes for product claims.
The archive treats Cargo.lock, bun.lock, uv.lock, flake.lock, provider locks, and equivalent lock surfaces as governed truth that stale dependent claims when drifted.
The archive requires registered telemetry and eval attributes with type, owner, cardinality class, privacy class, and allowed surfaces.
The archive requires each tool or MCP action to carry schemas, risk class, approval, idempotency, telemetry, cleanup, and claim impact.
The archive requires an inspectable runtime surface for agent work while preserving CLI receipts as claim authority.
The archive requires artifact/cache/state/media/receipt/packet/lock/pid/port/tempdir classification before cleanup and deletion receipts for apply.
The archive requires update_goal to stay forbidden until current goal state, receipts, stack claim ceiling, product proof eligibility, and cleanup/protection status are verified.
The archive defines stack fast as the fastest meaningful local feedback command with only fast-feedback and changed-scope structural claim support.
The archive defines stack standard as serious source-local repair proof across language standards, DB checks, observability semantics, tool inventory, fixtures, receipts, and claim ceiling.
The archive defines stack release as the full release/product proof loop and ties release/product/final-packet support to current same-surface receipts.
The archive defines clean proof as isolated-cache, fresh-checkout, no-hidden-state proof with full standard validation.
The archive defines watch as observations only, never completion authority without current receipt verification and claim ceiling computation.
The archive defines resources prove as bounded memory, queue, process, pool, browser artifact, workflow backlog, and tool cleanup proof across the stack.
The archive requires GC plan, dry-run, apply, and verify with artifact classification and no blind deletion.

The archive defines stack receipt fields, surface digests, claim support/exclusions, issue/expiry, and staleness triggers across locks, schemas, laws, fixtures, tool registries, package/install/runtime, and observability config.
The archive states cache use is legal, cache concealment is illegal, warm-cache speed is not clean proof, and cache proof is cache-surface proof only.
